reading.partial: 1 row should be one “{{label}}”, but some IDs repeat
reading.unnamed: What one row stands for is not decided yet
reading.singletonUnnamed: The whole table becomes one record (what it stands for is not decided yet)
reading.catalog: A value kind — equal values become one record ({{count}} distinct values)

diagram.notLinkedYet: At this stage the edges are only what the ID shapes imply. The real links between kinds are decided on the next screen (item meanings).
diagram.controls: Diagram controls (zoom in, zoom out, fit)

key.fromN: The ID is decided by the combination of {{columns}}
key.noCandidates: The original file is not at hand, so no candidates can be offered. Put the file back, or have the AI think again.
key.noneBlocks: {{count}} kind(s) still have no way to build an ID. Pick one of the candidates above to continue.
key.containedIn: The ID contains {{columns}}, so it is counted as one record inside {{parents}}. Adding the next file cannot produce a duplicate ID.
key.containedInUnknown: Not confirmed to belong to any kind (re-attach the files to check the link)
key.catalogRule: This ID exists to connect, so it is made of the value alone. Adding a file name or card number would make a separate record per file — and it would no longer join anything.

ns.nameInvalid: IDs can only use letters, digits and hyphens (e.g. thermoelectric-2026). You will give the display name at the last step, “Publish”.
ns.baseProvisional: The web address at the front of every ID is still provisional ({{base}}). You can continue as is for trying things out or personal use. A permanent address others can cite is set in the server's configuration.

vocab.declared: Registered the well-known words ({{names}}) as standard words.
vocab.renamed: Registered the unfamiliar words ({{names}}) as new words for this data.
vocab.unresolved: The AI's ID recipe uses words with no agreed meaning ({{names}}). As it is, saving will fail.
vocab.fix: Register these words and fix it
vocab.declaredOwn: Registered where this dataset issues its IDs ({{names}}). The IDs themselves are unchanged.

filesGone: The files are not at hand, so re-checking, asking the AI again and adding kinds are unavailable. Use “{{back}}” below to drop the files again.
filesGoneReattach: The files are not at hand, so re-checking, asking the AI again and adding kinds are unavailable. Use “{{reattach}}” to drop the files again.
addedHint: Added a per-record kind. You can continue with this name (item meanings are checked on the next screen).
missingColumns: The columns the AI named are not in this table: {{columns}}
fixColumn: The column “{{wrong}}” the AI named is not in this table. Closest match: “{{suggestion}}” (tap to fix).

confirm.head: Please check these before continuing.
confirm.collides: “{{map}}” still gives several rows the same ID. If you continue, those rows are merged into one.
confirm.gap: “{{columns}}” will not be imported. Create the per-record kind before continuing?
confirm.missing: The ID of “{{map}}” uses columns this table does not have ({{columns}}). Continuing will make the import fail.
confirm.placeholder: The AI's ID recipe contains a part this screen cannot fix (a placeholder address). If you continue, the automatic fix will try to repair it.

kindMissing: What one row of this table is has not been decided yet. Look at the example below and name it (e.g. sample, measurement, observation).
removeTitle: Delete this kind from the design
gateHow: ⚠ marks something to check — usually IDs that overlap. Pick one of the candidates below, or fix it under “Write the ID recipe yourself”. If the reading itself is wrong, use “Make the AI think again”. When everything looks right, press “Continue with these IDs”.
twinKinds: {{names}} currently write the same record twice from the same columns. If they are copies of one thing, delete the one you do not need (🗑). If they are different things, that is fine — split the items with the “Carried by” picker and this notice goes away. Which it is, only you can decide.

zone.head: Which kind carries which item
zone.lead: The checkbox on the left gives that value its own ID — the place where the same value in another file or in outside data joins. The picker on the right changes which kind carries the item. The AI's recommendation is filled in.
zone.isCardId: The ID for the whole file
zone.cardMoved: This file's contents, and the choice of which values get an ID, are listed together above under “Which kind carries which item”.
zone.keyNote: A column marked “{{label}}” is already in use as that kind's ID. To use a different column, open “Write the ID recipe yourself” in the tabs below.
zone.droppedNote: {{count}} column(s) you chose not to take in on the meanings screen are not listed here (go back to change that).
zone.chooseSummary: More — which ones should be kinds? what if ⚠ appears?
zone.chooseYes: If any of these fit, making it a kind will save you later:
zone.chooseYes1: The outside world calls it by the same name — a DOI, a catalogue number, a standard classification code, an instrument, a person, an organisation, a place, a material
zone.chooseYes2: You will want to say something about the value itself — as a plain item it can never carry facts of its own
zone.chooseYes3: Two or more kinds need to refer to it — as a plain item only one of them can have it (writing it on both puts the same fact in two places)
zone.chooseNo: Values that only mean something inside this file (a free-text note, a local serial) and measured numbers themselves are fine as plain items.
zone.chooseDoubt: If unsure, it is fine to leave things on “the whole file” for now. Until you publish, you can come back to this screen and change everything — add kinds, remove them, move items. Only after publishing, when IDs have been handed out, do they become immovable.
zone.diagramNote: Boxes are kinds. A solid line is one ID nested in another. A dotted line is one the machine adds next — kinds from one file always end up connected.
zone.diagramAria: A diagram of the shape this design makes. Boxes are kinds of data; arrows are the links between them.
zone.askSplit: Ask the AI how to split
zone.askSplitPrefill: How should the items in this table be split into kinds?
zone.askLinkPrefill: Which values would join with outside data? Which items should get an ID?
zone.askDup: Ask the AI about the duplicate
zone.askDupPrefill: The gate says {{names}} build the same record from the same columns. I want to judge whether they are copies of one thing or different things. Looking at the columns of this table, tell me concretely which to keep — or whether to split the items instead
zone.addSameId: + Add a kind with the same ID
zone.addSameIdHint: Name the new kind — same rule as ②: letters and digits, starting with a letter. After adding it, move items onto it with the “Carried by” picker on the right.
zone.addSameIdName: Name of the new kind (letters and digits, starting with a letter)
zone.addSameIdPlaceholder: letters and digits, starting with a letter
zone.addSameIdLead: Right now the value of {{key}} is the ID of one kind. Adding another kind with the same {{key}} as its ID lets you split different things mixed in one row (e.g. the measurement record and the thing that was measured) onto two kinds.
zone.missingCard: This table has no “one per file” kind yet. The {{count}} column(s) written once per file ({{first}}, …) are copied onto every record as designed now. The button below splits them into one entity keyed by {{key}}.

removeZoneHost: This kind holds the file-wide values. Deleting it also removes the “Which kind carries which item” list. If you only want a different ID column, use “Write the ID recipe yourself”.
kindsHead: Check that each ID points at one thing
kindsLead: For each kind you chose in ①, check its name and how its ID is built. Only the kinds marked ⚠ need your attention. Until you publish, you can change these as often as you like.
kindNameNote: This name says WHAT each record is, and is what people search and cite by (the text inside the ID is set separately, under “Write the ID recipe yourself”). Write it in letters and digits, starting with a letter (e.g. ChemicalFormula). Until you publish, both the name and the ID can be changed as often as you like.
kindNameRule: This name cannot be used. Spaces and symbols are not allowed, and non-Latin names become unreadable in the diagram. Use letters and digits, starting with a letter.
removeRowKind: This kind is where the per-record values ({{columns}}) live. Deleting it leaves them with nowhere to go. Afterwards an “Add the record-level kind” button appears on this screen to restore it, but you will have to name it again.
removeTitleRowKind: Delete this kind from the design (the per-record values lose their home)
rethinkKeeps: The design you see now is handed over as-is, and only what you ask for is changed. Edits made on this screen (kind names, ID recipes, deletions, splits) are kept.
rethinkResets: Thinking again rebuilds the design from scratch. Edits made on this screen (kind names, ID recipes, deletions, splits) are not kept.
check1: How it splits into kinds — the boxes. Is this the right split for this table?
check2: The items on each — the lists inside the boxes. Is each item on the right kind?
check3: The counts — the “n 件” on each box. Is that how you meant to count?
graphLegend: Boxes = kinds of data (items and counts inside). Amber = link receptacles you ticked in “Links to the outside”. Solid lines = ID nesting (the child’s ID contains the parent’s). Dotted = references the machine adds on ingest (ticked items stay on their kind, carried as references).
provisionalKey: “{{column}}” is a provisional ID (nothing was named in “Links to the outside”, so the machine guessed). You can proceed as is — if it is wrong, pick another under “Fix names & IDs”.
fixHead: When the shape is wrong (fix it)
